payload.rationale: The most recent observed starting point is August 2026 starts at 1.275M SAAR (preliminary), down from a revised 1.309M in July, with permits falling to 1.394M from 1.433M. To resolve YES, the first-print September figure must rise about 2% (roughly +25K) above the August level. Monthly starts are noisy (typical month-to-month moves of 4-7%), so a move of this size is well within range in either direction; the question is largely about where the center of the distribution sits. Permits near 1.39M are consistent with starts hovering around 1.28-1.32M, which pulls the center slightly up toward the threshold. Against that, 30-year mortgage rates jumped from ~6.65% in late August to 6.95% by September 17, and permits are trending down, both pointing to softer builder activity, though rate effects on starts operate with a lag of a month or more. Balancing mean-reversion toward permit-implied levels against deteriorating financing conditions and a downward permit trend, I place the September median a bit below 1.30M and estimate roughly a 40% chance the first print exceeds 1.300M. Too high: the sharp rate spike and falling permits could produce a sub-1.25M print, and August itself may be revised in ways that don't affect resolution but signal weaker momentum. Too low: starts are volatile and frequently rebound after a soft month; multifamily starts can swing the headline by 50K+ in a single month, and the permit level supports a print near or above 1.30M.
limitations: September starts are unreleased; August is preliminary and subject to revision.
No fitted model; estimate relies on general knowledge of starts volatility and the permits-starts relationship.
Small evidence packet; no data on builder sentiment, multifamily pipeline, weather, or regional factors.
Mortgage rate pass-through to starts has uncertain lag.
